title: Streamflow inspection playbook — per-chunk metrics, span enrichment, and content-safe redaction
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: As customers adopt streaming responses with tool/function calling and structured outputs, we lack a consistent inspector pattern for per-chunk telemetry, enriched tracing spans that link to tool calls, and deterministic redaction rules that avoid leaking PII in logs and traces. This ticket defines and implements a playbook (small framework + defaults) for collecting chunk-level metrics, attaching span metadata for downstream correlation (tool calls, function results, routing fallback), and applying content-aware redaction at the boundary before logs/traces/metrics are emitted. Goal: enable reliable per-chunk SLO monitoring, actionable tracing for debugging tool integrations, and ensure no sensitive content escapes telemetry channels.
acceptance_criteria: Per-chunk metrics emitted for generation streams: chunk_latency_ms, chunk_token_count, chunk_kv_cache_hit (bool), and chunk_sequence_index
Tracing: each chunk attaches a span with chunk_id, parent_request_id, active_tool_call_id (if any), and model_variant metadata; spans can be correlated to tool-call spans in distributed traces

Redaction: a pluggable redaction pipeline runs at the stream boundary and strips or masks PII per policy before metrics/tags/logs are exported; default policy blocks credit-card-like patterns, SSNs, and long bearer tokens
Compatibility: feature can be toggled per-route via API flag and gracefully degrades when legacy clients do not send chunk headers
Performance: end-to-end added p90 latency overhead for streaming requests < 2 ms per chunk on average in benchmark env
Docs & example: Console docs, SDK example (Node + Python) and an internal runbook for investigating stream incidents are published
tasks: Design: define chunk schema, metric names, and span attributes (small ADR)
Runtime: implement chunk inspector hook that can observe token boundaries and emit metrics asynchronously
Tracing: instrument span enrichment and implement correlation with tool-call spans (propagate tool_call_id)
Redaction: implement pluggable redaction pipeline with policy config and safe defaults
Compatibility layer: ensure older streaming clients are handled with graceful fallback and feature-flag gating
E2E tests: functional tests for metrics, spans, and redaction; performance microbenchmarks
Docs: publish PRD + Console playbook + SDK examples
Rollout: staged rollout with canary and observability gates
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive redaction reduces diagnostic fidelity — we will land with conservative defaults and provide a customer-configurable allowlist for enterprise tenants behind compliance review
Metric cardinality: do not attach freeform text to metrics. Any contextual text must be hashed or sent as trace attributes with redaction applied
Span volume: adding a span per chunk increases trace volume. We will provide sampling rules and a join-key for rehydrating traces when sampled
Compatibility: older SDKs send 'stream-chunk' frames without chunk-index metadata; inspector must synthesize chunk index deterministically (e.g., increment)

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Trace volume and cost increase when enabling chunk-level spans. Mitigation: default sampling (1%) and user-configurable sampling + group-by logic to rehydrate on demand.
Risk: Redaction may remove useful debugging context. Mitigation: keep a hashed fingerprint that can be appended to a secure diagnostics bucket accessible only to support with customer's approval.
Risk: Metric cardinality explosion if route-level or custom tags are unbounded. Mitigation: enforce tag schemas and reject high-cardinality labels at ingestion time
implementation_notes: Hook placement: after tokenizer/writer boundary but before socket emission — gives accurate token counts and allows synchronous redaction of final emitted payload
Redaction engine: use existing sanitizer library with streaming mode; fallback to chunk-level regex + entropy heuristics
Correlation: persist chunk_id -> span_id mapping in in-memory map with TTL that is scrubbed after request completes
Backward compatibility: when no chunk_id is present, synthesize from request_id + incremental counter and set header 'x-stream-chunk-synthesized: true'
